(Judgment of the Court was delivered by S.M.SUBRAMANIAM,J.)
The Writ Appeal has been instituted against the order dated 01.09.2022 passed in W.P.(MD).No.15526 of 2019.
2. The writ petitioner is the appellant before us.

The appellant states that without acquiring the land belonged to the appellant, the authorities of https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis the National Highways Department laid road and compensation also has not been paid.
Thus, the appellant was constrained to move the Writ Court.

3. When the matter was taken up by the Writ Court, the learned Additional Government Pleader made a submission that an award has been passed and the compensation amount of Rs.13,91,754/-
is ready for disbursal in favour of the appellant.
Accordingly, the learned Single Judge directed the respondents to serve the copy of the award on the writ appellant forthwith and without any delay.
The compensation was also directed to be settled in favour of the writ appellant.

Not satisfied with the order, the writ petitioner preferred the appeal on the ground that the damages, as sought for,
has not been granted by the Writ Court.
More so, the compensation awarded is not just and proper.

4. During the course of arguments, we found that the award has not been served on the writ appellant, since the respective learned counsels are unable to furnish the date of serving of the award to the writ appellant.
